result.title: Fair Recommender Systems for Intersecting Groups
result.summary: Recommendation systems that optimize for the average user can fail to capture the preferences of diverse demographic groups. We consider a dynamic recommendation system, where arriving users can belong to different demographic groups. Importantly, these groups can intersect, and a user may belong to several groups. We first show that over time, any group-blind policy (which excludes all current-user group information) recommending $K \geq 1$ items incurs linear total regret under mild conditions. In turn, we introduce three group-aware algorithms based on the classical Upper Confidence Bound algorithm (UCB): i) Intersection-Fitting, which runs UCB on each intersection, but has a sublinear group- and intersection-level regret guarantee with an exponential dependence in the number of groups; and ii) two group-level heuristics, Inner-Outer UCB and Group-Item UCB which allocate different arms to different groups, and use a sleeping expert meta-learner to choose which active group's recommendation an intersection should inherit at any given time step. We provide experimental results on two datasets, Goodreads and BoardGameGeek, and highlight that our heuristics can be preferable to the intersection-fitting algorithm when intersection-level preferences are closely related to group-level preferences, but that intersection-fitting performs better when different intersections within a same group prefer different items.

AI.brief_summary: 研究交叉人口群体下的动态推荐公平性，证明 group-blind 策略会产生线性总 regret，并提出基于 UCB 的三种 group-aware 算法（Intersection-Fitting 与两种 group-level 启发式），在 Goodreads 和 BoardGameGeek 上比较其优劣条件。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用 sleeping expert 元学习器在多个活跃群体/交叠之间动态分配与选择推荐的机制，可能为 LVR 中在多个 latent 假设或视觉证据源间按延迟反馈做选择与切换提供可核查的借鉴，但任务领域距视觉推理较远。
